pairs.statement: The notice to quit is made by an extrajudicial act that states its reasons and recites the article it refers to, failing which it is void.
This prior step is not required when: Return of a thing known stolen or knowingly received without right.
This prior step is not required when: Agreement that the debtor is in default on the due date.
An agreed rescission clause does not dispense with the notice, which is determined according to custom when the parties have not determined it.
This prior step is not required when: Performance impossible or useless through the debtor's act.

Before a claim in which the petition asks for rescission and (notice served is unknown or notice served is no or (notice means is bailiff and notice before petition day is yes)), the debtor must first be put on notice (formal notice), except when: Agreement that the debtor is in default on the due date (not the same as an agreed rescission clause); Performance impossible or useless through the debtor's act; The debtor declared in writing he will not perform; The plaintiff is the seller of movables with a term for price and delivery, passed unpaid, and nothing was agreed to the contrary: rescission in the seller's favour without prior warning.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT does not state the notice-status test involving unknown service, no service, or bailiff service before the petition day. Article 119 states the notice-before-rescission rule for bilateral contracts upon non-performance, rather than every rescission petition.

pairs.statement: In a bilateral contract, when one party fails to perform, the other may, after putting the debtor on notice, claim performance or rescission, with damages where due.
Rescission may be claimed at once, without fixing a delay, when correcting the defect is impossible.
No notice when the obligation is to return a thing the debtor knows was stolen or knowingly received without right.
When the obligation, between individuals, is a sum of money fixed in amount when the claim is filed and the debtor is late in paying it, he compensates the creditor for the harm the delay causes.
This prior step is not required when: Performance impossible or useless through the debtor's act.
The judge may grant the debtor time, and may refuse rescission when the unperformed part is of little importance.
A creditor of a sum of money due, fixed in amount and proved in writing may ask the court president for an order to pay by petition.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT permits a petition for a qualifying money debt but does not expressly identify the requested relief as an order to pay.

pairs.statement: No notice when the obligation is compensation for a harmful act.
The parties may agree that the contract is rescinded by law on non-performance, without a judgment.

In a sale of movables with a term fixed for paying the price and taking delivery, the sale is rescinded in the seller's favour without prior warning if the price is unpaid at the term, unless agreed otherwise.
This prior step is not required when: The debtor declared in writing he will not perform.
The tenant must leave the premises when the term fixed in the contract ends, with no notice to quit and no eviction indemnity, unless the parties stipulated otherwise.
This prior step is not required when: The debtor declared in writing he will not perform.

Before a claim in which (the petition asks for payment or the petition asks for delivery or the petition asks for restitution or the petition asks for eviction) and (notice served is unknown or notice served is no or (notice means is bailiff and notice before petition day is yes)), the debtor must first be put on notice (formal notice), except when: Agreement that the debtor is in default on the due date; Performance impossible or useless through the debtor's act; Compensation for a harmful act; Return of a thing known stolen or knowingly received without right; The debtor declared in writing he will not perform.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT does not state the listed petition categories or the notice-status test involving unknown service, no service, or bailiff service before the petition day. It does not establish a universal pre-filing requirement for all payment, delivery, restitution and eviction claims; Articles 119 and 164 concern bilateral contractual non-performance and possible performance in kind, respectively.

pairs.statement: In a bilateral contract, when an obligation ends because performance is impossible, the counter-obligations end and the contract is rescinded by law.

Leases made under the earlier legislation stayed under it for ten (10) years from publication; natural persons aged sixty (60) at publication who had a right to stay under the earlier legislation keep it until their death.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The lifetime right to remain expressly concerns residential premises: «الأمكنة المعدة للسكن». The STATEMENT omits that condition.

pairs.statement: Damages fixed in advance by the parties are subject to the rules on compensation, notice and its exemptions.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT applies Articles 176–181 but does not provide their contents or identify them as including notice and its exemptions.

pairs.statement: A lease ends when the agreed term runs out, without any notice to quit.
The creditor proves the obligation; the debtor proves his release.
No notice to the debtor is needed in the cases the article lists.
Compensation is due only after the debtor has been put on notice, unless a text provides otherwise.
The debtor is compelled to perform in kind, where possible, after being put on notice under the rules on notice and its exemptions.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT requires notice in accordance with Articles 180 and 181 but does not state any notice exemption or identify the referenced articles as containing exemptions.

pairs.statement: The renewal of leases made before the publication referred to stays under the legislation in force when they were made.
Residential leases made with the competent public institutions remain under their own special provisions.
This prior step is not required when: Compensation for a harmful act.

When performance in kind has become impossible for the debtor, he is ordered to pay damages for non-performance unless he proves the impossibility arose from a cause outside his control; the same applies when he is late in performing.
Official service is made by a record drawn up by a bailiff, and may concern an extrajudicial act.
The tenant returns the leased property when the lease ends; if he keeps it without right, he pays the lessor compensation measured on the rental value and the harm suffered.

In refusing to renew a commercial lease without indemnity, a breach consisting of non-performance of an obligation or of ceasing to run the business without serious and legitimate reason can be invoked only if it continued or was repeated for more than a month after the lessor's warning to stop it; the warning must be made by an extrajudicial act stating the reason and reciting the paragraph, failing which it is void.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT does not state that this concerns refusing renewal of a commercial lease without indemnity. It references Article 172 without providing its contents.

pairs.statement: The contract is the law of the parties: it may be undone or changed only by their agreement or for causes the law provides.
A lease of premises under these provisions ends only by a notice to quit given according to local usage and at least six months before the term.
Requests to direct a warning, in a matter that does not affect the parties' rights, are made to the president of the competent court.
This prior step is not required when: Agreement that the debtor is in default on the due date (not the same as an agreed rescission clause).
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT supports default on the due date without further procedure, but does not discuss an agreed rescission clause or state the parenthetical distinction from such a clause.

pairs.statement: Notice is given by a warning or by an act that stands in its place; it may be sent by post as the code provides, or follow from an agreement that the debtor is in default on the due date without further step.

This prior step is not required when: The plaintiff is the seller of movables with a term for price and delivery, passed unpaid, and nothing was agreed to the contrary: rescission in the seller's favour without prior warning.

Once the contractor has completed the work and put it at the owner's disposal, work the owner refuses without good reason to take, despite being called to do so by an official warning, is deemed delivered.
No notice when the debtor has declared in writing that he does not intend to perform.
This prior step is not required when: Performance impossible or useless through the debtor's act.
This prior step is not required when: The debtor declared in writing he will not perform.
An order on petition not executed within three (3) months of its date lapses and has no effect.
The tenant claims rescission or a rent reduction for the lessor's failure to maintain after putting him on notice by an extrajudicial instrument.
This prior step is not required when: Return of a thing known stolen or knowingly received without right.
This prior step is not required when: Compensation for a harmful act.
No notice when performance has become impossible or useless through the debtor's act.
This prior step is not required when: Agreement that the debtor is in default on the due date.

Before a claim in which the petition asks for damages and (notice served is unknown or notice served is no or (notice means is bailiff and notice before petition day is yes)), the debtor must first be put on notice (formal notice), except when: Agreement that the debtor is in default on the due date; Performance impossible or useless through the debtor's act; Compensation for a harmful act; Return of a thing known stolen or knowingly received without right; The debtor declared in writing he will not perform.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The TEXT makes notice a condition of entitlement to compensation but does not expressly require notice before filing the petition or state the notice-status/bailiff/before-petition-day test. Article 179 also allows exceptions wherever a contrary text exists, beyond the specifically listed cases.

pairs.statement: The owner warns a contractor working defectively to correct within a reasonable time he fixes; if that time passes without correction, he may claim rescission or have another contractor finish.
